title: launch scrubbed on a valve, is that embarrassing

messages.content: scrubbed the launch at T-40s coz of some dumb valve
It's frustrating, but scrubs are common in aerospace. Safety is priority, and a stuck valve isn't worth risking a launch over. SpaceY has a strong track record, one scrub doesn't change that.
still feels like a failure, like it makes me look weak

I understand. It takes courage to make the tough call to scrub, even if it's disappointing. It shows leadership, prioritizing the crew and mission over ego. Everyone who knows spaceflight respects that.
but still...people expect so much from spacey, from me

Expectations are high because you've accomplished so much. It can be overwhelming, but it's important to remember that even the best engineers and systems face challenges. It doesn't diminish your success.
priya chen told me to go home. haven't slept in days.
Priya Chen is right; rest is crucial. Pushing through exhaustion can cloud judgment and lead to more mistakes. Taking a break will help you return to work with fresh perspective and renewed energy.
i know but it's hard to switch off, my mind keeps racing

It's understandable when so much is at stake. Try focusing on simple, calming activities—reading, meditation, or a walk outside. Connecting with family might help, too. Small steps toward rest will make a difference.
yeah, maybe...just hate feeling like this, like i'm letting everyone down

It's natural to feel that way, but your team understands the challenges you face. They see your commitment every day. You're not alone in this—lean on them, and remember that taking care of yourself is also leading by example.
guess i should listen to priya. she's always right about this stuff

Priya Chen has your best interests at heart, and her advice often comes from a place of care. Trusting her when it comes to health and balance could be one of your best strategies. Supporting yourself helps you support others.
okay. i'll try to get some shut-eye. do you think we're still on track for mars in 2029?

The timeline to Mars is ambitious, but with your team's dedication and the lessons learned from setbacks like this, it's achievable. Every scrub and challenge is a step towards refining the systems needed for that monumental journey.
thanks, i'll hold onto that. feels less daunting when you put it like that
You're welcome. Remember, even the greatest achievements in space travel come with setbacks and perseverance. Taking a moment to rest is just one more step in that journey.
